summary: Require distinct declared execution units and deterministic bounded-handoff chaining for credited Adaptive Execution passes, then revalidate the merged Adaptive Execution behavior under the corrected discipline.
reason: PR #5 revision 6 recorded five SEPARATED semantic stages as complete even though they were effectively evaluated within one assistant response. The correction adds deterministic enforcement of unique declared execution-unit/boundary identities, ordered handoff chaining, closed historical exemptions, gate-before-pass chronology, historical identity uniqueness, immutable completed-pass evidence, and current artifact-state binding for partial subdivided completion. Revision-8 Adversarial found and corrected four successive defects: omission of the PR base snapshot from historical identity checks; mutation of execution identity after durable completion; an inability to represent subdivided execution honestly because subpasses were only recognized after the enclosing stage result became passing; and failure to validate a partial subpass completion against the current governed artifact state before that handoff could be consumed. Procedure-coverage assessment determined that these findings exposed reusable attack classes that were not explicit enough in the Adversarial authority. references/adversarial-review.md now explicitly requires workflow representability, post-credit immutability, intermediate-state validation, historical/base-state interaction, and a procedure-coverage classification after every material Adversarial finding. Because this authority change is governed behavior, Adversarial remains uncredited and the next semantic action is a fresh revision-8 Adversarial retry against the resulting artifact state. The repository still does not claim to prove a ChatGPT message/context boundary unless the host supplies a trustworthy boundary ID.
